# Section template

Purpose: the literal AGENTS.md skeleton contextify targets, with per-section line budgets, what each section may cite as evidence, and the tests that decide whether a line earns its place.

## The skeleton

Every physical line counts toward a section's allowance, including the heading, comments, and blank lines. A section with no evidence is omitted entirely: no heading, no placeholder, no TODO. (Source: DECISIONS.md D1.)

```markdown
# <project name>
<!-- contextify:begin v1 -->
<!-- Generated by contextify {toolVersion}; writer={generatedBy}; at={generatedAt}; commit={commit}; regenerate: /contextify update -->

<!-- 14 lines. evidence: package.json#scripts, Makefile/justfile targets, pyproject [project.scripts], Cargo bins, CI run: lines with working directories -->
## Commands
- Install: `<command>`
- Build: `<command>`
- Test: `<command>`
- Single test: `<command>`, or "Single test: unverified" when only the runner is known
- Lint / typecheck: `<command>`

<!-- 12 lines. evidence: two or more implementation files plus the relation between them, e.g. entry point to router to persistence -->
## Architecture
- `<path A>` to `<path B>`: <the relation between them>

<!-- 6 lines. evidence: tsconfig paths/strict/target, package.json#type, existing contributor instructions. never a rule a formatter owns -->
## Conventions
- <a rule not derivable from a linter config>

<!-- 6 lines. evidence: test config, fixtures, setup scripts, CI services:, .env.example keys a setup file references -->
## Testing
- <a quirk the test command alone does not reveal>

<!-- 4 lines. evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md, PR template, release workflow, default branch ref -->
## Repository workflow
- <a branch, PR, or release convention, sourced from a tracked file>

<!-- 8 lines. evidence: hazard detectors only, see detection-signals.md. whole section omitted when nothing fires -->
## Boundaries
- Always: <evidenced required action>
- Ask first: <evidenced action requiring approval>
- Never: <evidenced prohibited action, naming what to do instead>

<!-- 3 lines. evidence: existing doc paths, one task-specific reason to open each -->
## Read when relevant
- `<path>`: <the reason to open it for this task>

verified on {date} against {commit}
<!-- contextify:end -->
```

Two rules that apply across sections:

- **Architecture is the big picture that needs several files to understand.** Every bullet names at least two tracked paths and the relation between them; a directory listing, or a bullet naming only one file, does not qualify. (D1.)
- **The single-test line only appears when the working directory, the exact command, and a real example test path are all known.** With only the runner known, print `Single test: unverified` or omit the line. Never invent a filter flag. (D1.)

## Size scaling

| Class | Definition | Target lines | What's dropped |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Tiny | at most 10 eligible files, at most one build unit, no declared workspace | 20 | Architecture, Conventions, Testing, Repository workflow; necessary test detail folds into Commands instead |
| Medium | everything that is neither tiny nor a monorepo | 40 | nothing structural |
| Monorepo | at least two build units joined by workspace config, or documented as separately operated | 60 | nothing structural; Architecture typically uses more of its allowance |

Ceiling for the whole file: **150 lines**, hard, regardless of class. Scaling only goes down: a target is a goal, the ceiling refuses. Boundaries survives at any size when a hazard actually fires (D4); it is not subject to the "tiny drops it" rule. (Source: DECISIONS.md D2.)

## Worked example: tiny (fixture)

Fixture values, not a real repository.

```markdown
# demo-cli
<!-- contextify:begin v1 -->
<!-- Generated by contextify 0.1.0; writer=claude-opus; at=2026-09-16T10:00:00Z; commit=a1b2c3d; regenerate: /contextify update -->

## Commands
- Install: `npm install`
- Build: `npm run build`
- Test: `npm test`
- Single test: `npm test -- src/cli.test.ts`

## Boundaries
- Never: commit a real value into `.env`, `.env.example` is the tracked template

## Read when relevant
- `README.md`: setup and usage, this file only covers what README omits

verified on 2026-09-16 against a1b2c3d
<!-- contextify:end -->
```

18 physical lines, under the 20-line tiny target, with no Architecture, Conventions, Testing, or Repository workflow section. Boundaries is present only because a hazard fired: a tracked `.env.example` with `.env` gitignored.

## Worked example: medium (fixture)

Fixture values, not a real repository.

```markdown
# acme-web
<!-- contextify:begin v1 -->
<!-- Generated by contextify 0.1.0; writer=claude-opus; at=2026-09-16T10:00:00Z; commit=9f3e2ab; regenerate: /contextify update -->

## Commands
- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build: `pnpm run build`
- Test: `pnpm run test`
- Single test: `pnpm run test -- src/lib/pricing.test.ts`

## Architecture
- `src/app/api/checkout/route.ts` calls `src/lib/stripe.ts`, which writes to `src/lib/db.ts`
- `src/lib/db.ts` wraps the Postgres client from `prisma/schema.prisma`; every server action goes through it

## Conventions
- `tsconfig.json` sets `strict: true` and a `@/*` alias to `src/*`, use the alias, not `../../..`

## Testing
- `vitest.config.ts` loads `.env.test`; tests touching `src/lib/db.ts` need `DATABASE_URL` set

## Repository workflow
- Default branch is `main`, per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `push: branches: [main]` trigger

## Boundaries
- Always: run `pnpm run typecheck` before opening a PR, it is the `pull_request` gate in CI
- Ask first: touching `prisma/migrations/`, it runs against shared staging on merge
- Never: commit a real value into `.env`, `.env.example` is the tracked template

## Read when relevant
- `docs/architecture.md`: the full request lifecycle, this section only summarizes it

verified on 2026-09-16 against 9f3e2ab
<!-- contextify:end -->
```

33 physical lines, near the 40-line medium target and well inside the 150-line ceiling, with every section populated at least once.

## The removal test

Claude Code's own experimental init flow states the rule plainly: every line must pass the test of whether removing it would cause the agent to make a mistake; if not, cut it. (Source: research file `08-steal-list.md`, Claude Code experimental interactive prompt, Phase 4.) Applied to three example lines:

| Line | Kept or cut | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Single test: \`pnpm run test -- src/lib/pricing.test.ts\`` | Kept | Without it, an agent asked to run one test either invents a filter flag or reruns the whole suite; removing it causes a real mistake. |
| `This project uses React and TypeScript for the frontend.` | Cut | `package.json` already states this; removing the line changes nothing an agent would get wrong, since it can read the manifest directly. |
| `Write clean, readable code.` | Cut | Generic and not actionable; there is no concrete mistake this line prevents, and no repo evidence backs it. |
